ranked.headline: Quantum learning models shift toward feedback-free training and learned circuit design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints address QML trainability, kernel concentration and scaling via autonomous optimization, contractive layers and learned architecture search.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is making quantum learning models trainable and scalable beyond standard variational gradient loops. One scheme performs Riemannian gradient optimization autonomously, without measurements or classical feedback. A fully quantum Transformer combines SVD-based non-unitary circuits with quantum nonlinear activations and is trained by multi-agent RL without backpropagation. On trainability, an empirical study of fidelity and projected quantum kernels and quantum extreme learning examines how entanglement, locality and bandwidth scaling affect exponential concentration. On expressivity, contractive layers add all-to-all couplings governed by a single trainable parameter on Rydberg arrays. Architecture design is itself increasingly learned. LatentRL-QAS transfers circuit designs across qubit counts via latent-space RL, and an ML workflow extrapolates gate, measurement and reset syntax to scale holographic circuits. Adjacent work covers a dephasing-based minimum-complexity quantum reservoir, JEPA world models that infer Hamiltonian parameters, single-ancilla exponential advantage for multi-time correlators, and a QCBM prior guiding classical network training. All are preprints.

ranked.headline: Displacement field, stacking and twist steer valley order and Berry curvature in graphene
ranked.summary: New preprints link displacement-field control, layer number and twist to anomalous Hall metals, hysteresis and valley-imbalanced superconductivity in graphene.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is control of band topology and valley/pseudospin order in graphene multilayers via displacement field, stacking and twist. In ABA trilayer graphene, a displacement field inverts band edges, reverses Berry curvature and produces valley splitting. Experiments on Bernal pentalayer graphene report displacement-field-tunable first-order transitions with hysteretic Hall responses. Hartree-Fock work on Bernal tetralayer graphene predicts interaction-driven ordering of multiple pseudospins and anomalous Hall metals. In 17-layer rhombohedral graphene, superconductivity with valley-imbalanced Fermi pockets is enhanced by in-plane field. In twisted monolayer-N-layer rhombohedral graphene, narrow topological bands arise from Dirac-cone/surface-state hybridization tuned by layer number. Magic-angle twisted bilayer work finds hidden f-wave TIVC order near nu=-2, and Floquet driving is predicted to induce valley polarization and Chern transitions. Parallel lines treat twisted TMDs (an angle-independent microscopic continuum model; a non-quantized Chern metal in a holon model) and 3D quantum anomalous Hall systems from coupled Weyl semimetals. All are preprints.

ranked.headline: Shear, BAO and supernova combinations probe time-varying dark energy against ΛCDM
ranked.summary: New HSC-Y3 shear, CMB acoustic-prior and model-comparison analyses test whether DESI-era hints of evolving dark energy survive alternative explanations.
ranked.synthesis: The main thread is whether combined late- and early-Universe data prefer dynamical dark energy over ΛCDM. HSC-Y3 cosmic shear combined with DESI BAO, DES SNe and BBN priors gives a 2.4σ preference for a time-varying equation of state. Allowing w0wa removes the hinted early-recombination preference from CMB+BAO and yields the lowest AIC, suggesting the two extensions compete for the same data features. A genetic-algorithm reconstruction of scalar-tensor Lagrangians fit to DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, CMB and fσ8 improves on ΛCDM by Δχ²=-16.6. Inputs and systematics are also being revisited. Updated CMB acoustic priors separate early-Universe information from lensing and ISW effects. DES supernova colour evolution constrains intergalactic dust that could shift distance moduli. Forecasts propose galaxy-CMB and galaxy-galaxy lensing ratios as geometric probes of dark energy and curvature for LSST and Simons Observatory. Separately, axion early dark energy combined with JWST high-redshift galaxy abundances gives H0≈72.76 km/s/Mpc.

ranked.headline: Quantum and classical methods push real-time many-body dynamics toward larger systems
ranked.summary: New preprints pair analog and digital quantum simulators of gauge, Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard and QCD-cascade dynamics with scalable classical solvers.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is simulation of real-time many-body dynamics, split between quantum-hardware encodings and classical methods. On the quantum side, a cold-atom analog simulator of a 1D SU(2) quantum link model observes coherent meson-baryon conversion under tunable mass and gauge parameters. A Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson circuit evolves the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model and is benchmarked against exact diagonalization. A coherent quantum-circuit encoding of finite-state Mueller dipole branching at small x is compared with continuous cascade fluctuations and H1 DIS data. On the classical side, cluster spin-LSC treats a sensor and strongly coupled bath spins quantum mechanically to model spin-qubit decoherence in large ensembles. Dirac propagation simulates local fermionic observables under particle-number-conserving unitaries. Transition path sampling is formulated for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion to extract rare-event rates in strongly coupled open systems. Separately, quantum Monte Carlo of 2D repulsive dipolar bosons (interlayer excitons) yields an analytical framework for chemical potential and interaction energies.

ranked.headline: Adaptive and hybrid solvers push correlated quantum dynamics and ground states further
ranked.summary: Seven preprints refine tensor-network, Gutzwiller, neural-state and QMC solvers, several drawing on quantum hardware or early-FTQC algorithms for input.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is methodological: extending the reach of correlated many-body simulations through adaptivity or quantum-classical hybridization. On the classical side, adaptive multiset tree tensor networks adjust bond dimension per configuration to converge exciton dynamics in Holstein-type models. An adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller scheme carries Hubbard quench dynamics to longer times and matches DMFT references across coupling strengths. Thermofield dynamics combined with ML-MCTDH and finite-basis Bogoliubov transforms treats anharmonic Morse baths for vibrational relaxation. For neural quantum states, an implicit-Euler stochastic reconfiguration underpins implicit augmented imaginary-time evolution. Hybrid work includes Rydberg-array measurements used to pretrain RBM and RNN guiding wavefunctions for projective QMC. Another hybrid proposal is an early-FTQC algorithm that estimates small energy differences, such as molecular forces, with lower sampling cost than phase estimation. A third embeds quantum-assisted ground-state estimation in simulated annealing to find compact bases for ab initio many-fermion problems.

ranked.headline: Moiré superlattices tune polaritons and phonons; metasurface quasi-BICs run in parallel
ranked.summary: Preprints report spectroscopic evidence of moiré-mediated electron-phonon coupling and gate-tunable polaritons in graphene systems, alongside tunable quasi-BIC metasurfaces.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is moiré control of hybrid excitations in graphene-based systems. In twisted bilayer graphene studied from AB stacking to 5.5°, hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons show gate-tunable wavelengths through remote moiré effects. In graphene/hBN superlattices, a Fano resonance is reported as the first direct observation of coupling between moiré flat-band electronic excitations and hBN out-of-plane optical phonons. Helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy identifies reconfigurable chiral phonons in asymmetrically stacked graphene moiré superlattices. Three metasurface preprints form a looser parallel strand: THz collective flatbands with zero group velocity, polarization-independent strong coupling between Brillouin-zone-folding quasi-BICs and A excitons in bulk WS2, and liquid-crystal tuning of anisotropy-induced quasi-BICs. The new element is direct spectroscopic evidence of moiré-mediated interlayer coupling alongside demonstrated tunability.

ranked.headline: Tailored high-dimensional, entangled and squeezed-light states from photonic and circuit platforms
ranked.summary: Six preprints extend engineered nonclassical light across OAM, spatial, microwave and squeezed-vacuum regimes, spanning 128-dimensional OAM and on-demand biphotons.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is engineering the state of light through its degrees of freedom or its driving nonclassical resource. Three preprints address spatial and OAM encoding: 128-dimensional single-photon OAM comb states with sum-frequency upconversion from telecom to 520 nm, phase-only hologram tailoring of OAM amplitude and phase, and a brighter high-dimensional spatially entangled pair source from beam-like Type-II SPDC in BBO with ~1.45x coincidence gain. Three theoretical proposals use other resources: frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer, emitter scattering of squeezed vacuum for cat-cluster-state generation, and phase matching of high-order harmonics driven by coherent plus bright squeezed vacuum. The items pair dimensionality scaling with brightness and wavelength conversion, alongside squeezed-light and circuit-QED schemes. They are heterogeneous in platform, and the summaries do not establish a shared characterization emphasis.

ranked.headline: Differentiable forward models and validated emulators for survey-scale cosmological inference
ranked.summary: SPHEREx, 21-cm, Lyman-alpha and Euclid papers advance differentiable, emulated or automated components of inference pipelines for upcoming survey analyses.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is building and validating components of survey inference pipelines, with emphasis on differentiable or emulated forward models. Hesperos and Eosphoros provide a GPU-accelerated differentiable forced-photometry operator and forward model for SPHEREx spectrophotometry, while a separate SPHEREx study introduces information-criterion-driven non-linear deprojection of angular imaging systematics, tested on lognormal mocks. A differentiable GPU-accelerated hybrid forward model for global 21-cm cosmology supports uncertainty-quantification benchmarking. Symbolic regression diagnoses a Lyman-alpha GP emulator, and a Sobolev loss improves derivative fidelity for most cases. Lens-Orchestra automates strong-lens forward modeling with LLM agents on 185 Euclid Q1 candidates. The Popcorn Void Finder reimplementation is a reproducibility effort, less directly tied to differentiability.

ranked.headline: Decoders, verified compilers, and hardware-aware simulation target the classical layer of FTQC
ranked.summary: Six preprints from 20–25 Nov 2026 address FTQC's classical stack: real-time decoding, verified compilation, speculative execution, and trapped-ion QEC modeling.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the classical software and control stack required to run fault-tolerant quantum computation. Two decoder papers address throughput and noise realism: a GPU decoder for bivariate bicycle codes sustains one syndrome round per microsecond under circuit-level noise, and a loss-aware CNN decoder with a fast sampler lowers logical error rates for qubit loss in surface and high-rate qLDPC codes. On compilation, QBlue's machine-checked Hamiltonian simulation compiler is extended to block-encoding algorithms, and LLM-driven search cuts the expected Toffoli count for RSA-2048 factoring by up to 78.6%. Froq introduces speculative execution on live quantum states using recovery contracts, while THeatA adds per-ion phonon and heating tracking to QCCD trapped-ion QEC simulation. The common emphasis is verifiable, hardware-aware design.

ranked.headline: Symmetry and code structure are exploited to cut costs of quantum state-preparation and compilation
ranked.summary: Five preprints use symmetry, code structure, or constraints to reduce Toffoli counts and circuit resources in state preparation, compilation, and magic-state factories.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is circuit construction that exploits explicit structure to reduce resource cost. Two preprints prepare DMRG matrix product states by using spin symmetry: abelian-symmetric block-sparse protocols cut Toffoli counts by up to 135x, and a non-Abelian SU(2) approach uses Wigner-Eckart reduction and Clebsch-Gordan transforms. CSS-T-Product codes, whose transversal phase gates implement multi-qubit logical diagonal gates, enable tailored magic-state factories. A structure-aware compiler with persistent occupancy encoding preserves constraints for independent-set optimization circuits. PP-VarQITE combines Pauli propagation with variational imaginary-time evolution for shallow thermal-state circuits, demonstrated on up to 98 qubits. The items address different circuit classes and do not share a single method; the common element is tying synthesis to symmetry or code structure.

ranked.headline: Tighter bounds and certification criteria for quantum resources under restricted access
ranked.summary: Five preprints sharpen device-independent, Pauli-limited, entropic, capacity and recovery-map bounds, refining how quantum resources are certified and limited.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is bounding or certifying quantum resources when access is constrained. For Q2222, the normal cone at every nonlocal extremal behaviour is constructed explicitly, with device-independent applications. In Pauli-limited channel certification, the stabilizer norm of the Choi state is shown not to fully determine robustness once positivity is imposed. Purity-based continuity bounds for qubit von Neumann entropy are sharp and extend to conditional entropy and mutual information, with machine-learning-assisted estimation. An amplitude-damping two-way capacity upper bound is strictly tighter than PLOB and related bounds. Pretty good measurements and Petz recovery maps are unified in a semidefinite programming framework with tunable power, yielding a stronger bound. The new elements are tighter, more explicit characterizations rather than new protocols.

ranked.headline: Preprints derive exact reachability and cost bounds for constrained quantum operations
ranked.summary: Five preprints give resource-specific bounds on control cost, state reachability and conversion under restricted quantum operations, from amplitude amplification to texture.
ranked.synthesis: The shared thread is determining what a restricted set of operations can achieve and at what resource cost. One preprint bounds the quantum-data copy cost of controlling amplitude amplification using no-signaling and distinguishability arguments, with quadratic scaling. Another analyzes reachability, geometry and preparation cost for multipartite states under differentiable collision-model control with partial-SWAP and Heisenberg exchange plus local phases. A third characterizes reachable effective observables of fixed-readout quantum neural networks under unitary, mixed-unitary and CPTP resources, with strict inclusions. A fourth shows eight labels suffice for interface choices in hybrid correlation generation with finite shared randomness. The fifth gives an exact deterministic conversion criterion for mixed states in quantum-state texture, derived from a complete characterization of free operations. The common advance is sharp, resource-specific boundaries rather than generic capability claims.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-defined orbital, odd-parity and polar orders predicted to yield Hall and transport responses
ranked.summary: Five preprints derive Hall-type and charge-spin responses from symmetry-defined order, including orbital-only and field- or stacking-tunable mechanisms.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is theoretical derivation of measurable responses from symmetry-defined order, without conventional spin magnetization as the starting point. Odd-parity magnets are assigned charge-spin selection rules with temporal-spectral separation. In monolayer H-phase MoS2, an orbital exchange field gives an intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity without spin magnetism or spin-orbit coupling. Twisted bilayer NiPS3 is predicted to host p-wave spin textures reoriented by a perpendicular electric field. Sliding antiferroelectric four-layer MoS2 is predicted to show a quantum-metric-driven nonlinear valley Hall effect, and axial ferrons in uniaxial ferroelectrics thermal and angular-momentum Hall effects. New relative to a pure spin picture are the orbital-only mechanisms and electric-field or stacking tunability. All five are preprints based on theory or first-principles calculations.

ranked.headline: Electronic-structure models extended to fields, correlation, and coupled dynamics
ranked.summary: Four preprints extend electronic-structure modeling to external fields, singlet-state correlation, coupled ion-electron dynamics, and exciton-phonon workflows.
ranked.synthesis: The four preprints extend electronic-structure descriptions beyond standard ground-state treatments through learned models, reduced models, functional parameterization and workflow codes. MLEH-LR adds long-range interactions and external fields to a machine-learning electronic Hamiltonian, applied to boron nitride ribbons. The TAO-DFT work proposes a nonempirical, spin-symmetry-restoration scheme that sets a system-dependent fictitious temperature for lowest singlet states of molecules. LeIFF treats valence electrons as dynamical spherical charge distributions in a compact force field for coupled nuclear and electronic dynamics at large scale. LetzElPhC is an open-source code that computes electron-phonon and exciton-phonon matrix elements from Quantum ESPRESSO DFPT output and interfaces with Yambo. The common thread is broader physical scope at controlled computational cost.

ranked.headline: Field-level mappings extend N-body and hydrodynamic simulations to new forests, dark energy and dark matter
ranked.summary: New preprints validate field-level shortcuts against reference runs for Lyman-alpha mocks, dark energy expansion histories and scalar-field dark matter initial conditions.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is extending costly simulations through field-level mappings and checking them against reference runs. A 3D U-Net maps density and velocity fields to Lyman-alpha flux, reproducing P1D, bispectrum and trispectrum across IllustrisTNG and FLAMINGO. Two papers argue that N-body dynamics depend only on the expansion history a(τ), so constant-w simulations can reproduce CPL and more general w(z) models; one reports agreement within 0.2% in power. The scalar-field dark matter paper is distinct in focus: it builds matched LCDM-SFDM initial conditions linking CLASS-SFDM, MUSIC and AxioNyx, and finds that accurate density recovery does not guarantee adequate wave-phase resolution. Validation criteria therefore matter as much as the mapping itself.

ranked.headline: Spectroscopic and lensing surveys map galaxy, quasar and baryon tracers of structure
ranked.summary: New DESI, HSC-SSP and JWST survey analyses constrain protoclusters, cluster lensing mass, group baryons and LRD abundance at cosmic noon.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of wide-area survey data to characterize structure tracers across cosmic time, at different scales and with differing statistical strength. DESI DR1 physical quasar pairs at z≈2, separated by up to 2.5 Mpc, trace protocluster environments consistent with ΛCDM mock predictions. VENUS provides strong-lensing models for 57 JWST clusters, with 1733 multiply-imaged systems, and derives mass scaling relations. Localized FRBs crossmatched with DESI galaxy groups yield a tentative 143 pc cm^-3 excess dispersion measure along group-intersecting sight lines, a low-significance result. An HSC-SSP spectroscopic search finds Little Red Dot number density falling ~35x from z~4-8 to z~2.1-2.6, while the optical luminosity-function knee does not evolve. The items probe distinct tracers rather than a single common observable.

ranked.headline: Simulation-informed hybrid bias models extended to reconstruction, baryons and primordial non-Gaussianity
ranked.summary: Four preprints from 19–25 November 2026 extend simulation-calibrated bias descriptions to post-reconstruction clustering, diffuse baryons, b_φ priors and gas prediction.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the pairing of simulation inputs with compact bias parameterisations for large-scale-structure observables. The hybrid Lagrangian bias expansion is extended to post-reconstruction galaxy clustering, where a combined pre- and post-reconstruction analysis improves cosmological constraints. A hybrid effective field theory for diffuse baryons combines N-body displacements, a Lorentzian feedback suppression and linear bias. For primordial non-Gaussianity, a flexible subhalo abundance matching model fit to small-scale clustering, with separate-universe simulations, constrains the bias parameter b_φ. CosmoMap is methodologically distinct: a conditioned 3D U-Net predicts hot gas temperature and electron density from dark matter fields in CAMELS IllustrisTNG, offering a learned rather than parametric route to baryonic tracers.

ranked.headline: Validated halo, N-body and likelihood tools target Stage IV survey precision and scale
ranked.summary: New halo-modelling and N-body tools target Stage IV accuracy and LSST-scale data volumes with validation against established codes and fits.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is computational infrastructure linking dark matter halo evolution to survey observables. SciPIC-lite provides a public Python pipeline for flexible Halo Occupation Distribution modelling aimed at clustering observables, validated by fitting. PhotoNs-3 is tested against GADGET for accuracy and convergence in power spectra, halo profiles and mass functions, framed around Stage IV requirements. A separate N-body scheme for self-interacting dark matter uses distance-threshold interactions that depend on relative velocity and time step, targeting enhanced spatial resolution and performance. The supernova Woodbury factorization paper is related mainly through scale, reducing LSST-scale fit time from about 10 weeks to about 1.5 hr. Collectively, the emphasis is on validated, tractable pipelines rather than new halo-physics measurements.

ranked.headline: Foregrounds, calibration, and birefringence modeled as biases in CMB and 21 cm inference
ranked.summary: Four preprints quantify how CO foregrounds, polarization calibration, and cosmic birefringence bias CMB analyses, while DSL 21 cm forecasts target reionization parameters.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is explicit modeling of nuisance signals and instrumental effects that can bias cosmological inference. An analytic halo model for CO and its CIB cross-correlation finds CO adds roughly 2σ bias to cosmological parameters in CMB-HD-like settings. A Simons Observatory study uses simulations to compare methods for transferring absolute polarization-angle calibration between the LAT and SAT. Another paper shows unmodeled anisotropic cosmic birefringence positively biases small-scale CMB lensing bandpowers and uses joint MUSE estimation of lensing and birefringence to address it. The 21 cm item is a forecast rather than a systematics study: Bayesian inference of cosmic dawn and reionization parameters from simulated DSL lunar-orbit global spectra, combined with HERA/SKA-Low data.

ranked.headline: Metasurfaces program polarization topology and coherence in space-time structured classical light
ranked.summary: Four preprints from late November 2026 link knotted polarization, terahertz toroidal pulses and entanglement-like coherence through spatiotemporal metasurface control.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is spatiotemporal structure treated as a programmable degree of freedom in classical electromagnetic fields, with polarization as the main carrier. One preprint constructs vectorial wavepackets whose Stokes trajectories are linked or knotted. Another generates and tunes toroidal terahertz pulses with transient vectorial photocurrents in a graphene optoelectronic metasurface. Two space-time metasurface works program coherence: one synthesizes polarization states into quantum-inspired bits across 48 resolved channels, and the other realizes Bell- and GHZ-like multipartite states. The terahertz work shares the topological theme but uses a different generation route. What is new is the shift from static polarization topology toward joint control of topology, coherence and temporal structure within classical light.

ranked.headline: Searches for primordial oscillatory features and ultralight dark matter couplings
ranked.summary: Current Planck PR4, BOSS/eBOSS and NANOGrav 15-year data now constrain oscillatory primordial features and ultralight dark matter couplings.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread in these items is the use of precision cosmological and astrophysical datasets to search for signatures of physics beyond the standard model. Two preprints target oscillatory features in the primordial power spectrum. One examines axion monodromy inflation against Planck PR4, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ and ACT/SPT data. The other performs a full-shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and eBOSS quasars combined with Planck PR4 CMB data and reports no significant evidence for primordial oscillatory features. The third preprint is distinct in domain: it uses timing data from 50 NANOGrav 15-year binary pulsars to constrain ultralight dark matter couplings to matter through orbital resonance perturbations. What is new is the joint use of Planck PR4 with DESI DR2 BAO and full-shape BOSS/eBOSS analyses for the feature search, and the application of pulsar orbital dynamics to ultralight dark matter couplings.

ranked.headline: Single-shot and coded methods recover wavefronts in turbulent and disordered optics
ranked.summary: Three new preprints propose single-shot or coded routes to wavefront recovery in turbulent and disordered optical systems.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is recovering wavefront information in disordered or turbulent optical systems, where spatially varying phase and field-dependent point-spread functions complicate conventional reconstruction. The anisoplanatic blind deconvolution preprint places a pupil-plane spatial light modulator with known phase codes in the optical path, enabling joint recovery of the image and spatially varying turbulence phases. The holographic-gradient preprint derives the loss gradient from a single off-axis hologram, which supports in situ training of optical systems through disorder. The deep-learning preprint reconstructs multiple wavefronts from one speckle pattern produced by a thin diffuser, using recurrent all-pairs field transforms and Zernike regression. Two of the three rely on single-shot or single-pattern acquisition. All three are preprints, and the items do not present quantitative comparisons among them.

ranked.headline: Geometry and stacking choices control otherwise suppressed responses in 2D systems
ranked.summary: Recent preprints show that lattice geometry, interface orientation, and layer stacking set electronic and optical responses in two-dimensional systems.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is geometry and symmetry as controls of response in two-dimensional electronic systems. arxiv:2611.28213 is a tight-binding study of quantum-geometric nonlinear conductivity in SrTiO3 two-dimensional electron gases, comparing (001) and (111) interfaces, with multiorbital driving as the reported mechanism. arxiv:2611.30343 examines electronic and magnetic states in semi-Dirac quantum dots, where triangular and hexagonal geometries yield edge-asymmetric magnetism. arxiv:2611.34900 reports that rhombohedral stacking in 3R-MoS2 bilayers brightens spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons, identified through g-factors and resonant hybridization. The new element is the explicit link between geometric or stacking choices and a response that is otherwise forbidden, as in the brightening of forbidden excitons. The methods, systems, and observables differ, so the shared thread is geometry-controlled response rather than a common mechanism.

ranked.headline: Gain-loss balance and nonreciprocal coupling shape non-Hermitian spectral structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints constrain and extend how gain, loss, and nonreciprocal coupling can tune non-Hermitian eigenstate structure.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of gain-loss balance and coupling asymmetry as handles on non-Hermitian spectral structure. A preprint on time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with T symmetry shows that gain-loss induced symmetry breaking is forbidden even for random gain-loss distributions, establishing a constraint on such control. A second preprint introduces pseudo-altermagnetism, in which balanced gain and loss mimic altermagnetic spin splitting, with movable nodal structures. A third shows that tunable nonreciprocal coupling near a second-order polarization exceptional point produces state-selective eigenstate splitting, with one branch distinguished. The items are heterogeneous: one establishes a constraint while the other two describe control mechanisms. What is new is the specific combination of mechanisms and constraints rather than a single unified result.

ranked.headline: Embedding wave propagation physics into neural networks for optical inverse problems
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple wave-propagation physics with deep learning for diffractive inverse design and tomographic amplitude retrieval.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is the embedding of explicit wave physics into learned models for optical inverse problems. MSWNets combine fully connected networks with Rayleigh-Sommerfeld propagation in a PINN-inspired formulation to design broadband diffractive optics. Gradient optical diffraction tomography uses physics-informed deep learning, with a ResNet, to estimate the missing amplitude gradient, extending gradient-based tomography to amplitude retrieval. What is new in the two diffractive items is that propagation physics is built into the learning or estimation step itself. The AI-assisted topological high-harmonic study retrieves anisotropic nonlinear responses and crystal symmetries of atomically thin materials; it shares only the learning-for-inference element and addresses a different nonlinear light-matter regime.

ranked.headline: Coherent control in coupled cavities via nonlinearity, dissipation, and sideband driving
ranked.summary: Three recent theoretical preprints propose control schemes for driven cavity systems, and their summaries report no experimental validation.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a thread of engineering coherent control in driven, coupled cavity systems by tailoring a specific control resource. arxiv:2611.27200 derives analytic optimal conditions for unconventional photon blockade in coupled cavities with second-order nonlinearity and asymmetric dissipation, targeting robust antibunching. arxiv:2611.30645 proposes a Floquet sideband method for controlling mechanical dark modes in a three-mode optomechanical system, supported by fidelity and population analyses. arxiv:2611.32215 applies PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics with second-order sidebands and tunable slow-fast light to magnetometry, with theoretical picotesla-level sensitivity. What is new in each case is the explicit use of nonlinearity, asymmetric dissipation, Floquet driving, or PT symmetry as a control parameter. All three works are theoretical proposals, and their summaries report no experimental validation.

ranked.headline: Symmetry-protected phases and magnetic orders extended to new lattice settings
ranked.summary: Preprints extend topological and magnetic classification to half-chiral symmetry, spin space groups and fractal lattices.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is symmetry-constrained classification: the controlling symmetry, invariant or lattice setting is widened, and the resulting phases or magnetic orders are then enumerated or characterized accordingly. One preprint treats topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry, where chiral symmetry acts on a single sublattice, using real-space invariants and zero-energy modes. A second enumerates spin space groups via translation holonomy, yielding 17 spin-lattice types with neutron diffraction signatures; this classifies magnetic order rather than topological phases. A third realizes SSH, Haldane, Qi-Wu-Zhang and Z2 insulators on fractal lattices such as the Cantor set, hexaflake and Sierpiński carpet, including site-eliminated, projected and patterned constructions. What is new is the extension of protecting symmetries, invariants and lattice geometries rather than a single shared method.

ranked.headline: Metasurfaces and metagratings engineered for Jones-level polarization control
ranked.summary: Preprints pair mode-matching, topology optimization, and susceptibility bounds to specify metasurface polarization response.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is Jones-level control of polarization in metasurfaces and metagratings, pursued along two routes. arXiv:2611.27311 uses analytical mode-matching to design dielectric-loaded perforated metallic metagratings that achieve dual-polarized anomalous refraction, validated by full-wave simulation. arXiv:2611.28364 presents a differentiable topology optimization framework for polarization-analyzing gratings that removes the paraxial restriction of the Jones-Fourier formalism. arXiv:2611.34146 instead derives analytically tractable minimum effective-susceptibility bounds for realizing unitary and nonunitary Jones polarization transformations. The three items do not share a single methodology; the shared element is the attempt to specify polarization response either through numerical inverse design or through analytical limits on material response. What is new is the extension beyond paraxial treatments and the explicit bounding of achievable polarization transformations.

ranked.headline: Theory predicts Josephson and superconducting devices for detection and spin conversion
ranked.summary: Three recent preprints propose phase-coherent superconducting devices, with design predictions awaiting experimental tests.
ranked.synthesis: The common thread is phase-coherent control of charge, spin and thermal responses by superconducting or Josephson elements. A numerical study proposes a flux-driven DC-SQUID threshold detector whose nonequilibrium phase dynamics aim to reduce thermal noise while detecting microwave pulses near the single-microwave-photon energy scale. A theory proposal for a two-orbital quantum dot Josephson junction with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman splitting maps a temperature difference onto a phase difference, projected for noise-optimized thermometry. A third preprint argues that the inverse spin Hall effect in a superconductor could approach unity spin-to-charge conversion in a nonlocal spin-valve geometry. The new content is therefore design predictions rather than experimental demonstrations, since all three items are theoretical or numerical proposals.

ranked.headline: Dissipative soliton formation in microresonators, burst lasers and fiber lasers
ranked.summary: Recent preprints address turnkey Kerr soliton start-up and dispersion-imbalance removal in burst-mode lasers, alongside a review of fiber-laser solitons.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread is dissipative soliton dynamics, in which localized pulses and states persist through the interplay of dispersion, nonlinearity, and gain or loss. Two preprints address this on different platforms. One analyzes turnkey dissipative Kerr soliton generation in self-injection-locked photonic-crystal ring resonators using coupled Lugiato-Lefever equations. The other introduces dissipative erasure, a spectral-filtering and nonlinear-amplification scheme that removes pulse-to-pulse dispersion imbalance in ultrafast burst-mode lasers. The third item is a survey chapter on temporal solitons in mode-locked fiber lasers, including soliton molecules and dispersion-managed solitons. The items are heterogeneous: the two preprints are research contributions, while the chapter is a review. What is new is the explicit treatment of turnkey start-up in photonic-crystal microresonators and a spectral-filtering route to dispersion-imbalance removal in burst-mode lasers.

ranked.headline: Nonadiabatic tunneling and harmonic generation in driven correlated insulators
ranked.summary: Recent preprints report nonadiabatic tunneling and non-integer harmonic generation in light-driven correlated insulators.
ranked.synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is the nonadiabatic response of correlated insulators to light fields. Time-resolved optical spectroscopy of NiPS3 reports nonadiabatic quantum tunneling and ponderomotive blue-shifted resonances near the Keldysh regime. In the cuprate Mott insulator Sr2CuO3, experiment and simulation together show non-integer, blueshifted high harmonic generation under mid-infrared driving, attributed to many-body nonadiabatic gating. The third item is methodological: a Yb-laser-based time-resolved terahertz platform combining multi-pass-cell compression, spintronic THz generation and air-biased detection over a broad bandwidth. What is new is the joint treatment of tunneling and harmonic response in driven correlated insulators, probed with broadband, high-sensitivity techniques.

ranked.headline: Simulation-trained surrogates couple optical physics to design and inverse imaging
ranked.summary: Physics-based simulation now trains surrogates that link forward optics to design and inverse imaging tasks.
ranked.synthesis: The three preprints share a reliance on physics-based simulation to train or guide learned models for optical systems, although their roles differ. The incoherent multispectral diffractive optical network paper uses a surrogate-guided design approach for onboard satellite image classification, treating the optical hardware as a design variable. The scintillator detector paper trains a neural surrogate for light-guide photon transport via adjoint Monte Carlo sampling, making readout differentiable so that geometry and readout can be co-designed. DeepBlur, trained on physical simulations, instead addresses the inverse problem, blindly estimating spatially varying 2D point spread functions from single fluorescence microscopy images to improve deconvolution. The dominant thread is the surrogate-mediated coupling of physical models to computational optical imaging. What is new is the use of differentiable or simulation-trained surrogates to link forward physics with either design or inference, rather than a shared instrument or modality.
